headline: Meta has plugged its Muse AI agent into 15 business tools such as Shopify, QuickBooks and Stripe, and into Meta ad accounts, so small businesses in the US and Canada can have it work on their shops, books and ads.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the launch is from 29 Sep 2026 and our 10 Oct 2026 edition already carried it, so this piece adds analysis rather than a new event.
importance_line: Small-business owners in the US and Canada are affected first, since an agent can now read their store, books and ad data, then advertisers and agencies, then Meta, and the doubt is that Meta has not said whether the agent can change ad budgets, what paid plans cost or how business data is kept apart from its ad systems.
summary: PPC Land reports that Meta announced Muse for Small Business on 29 Sep 2026, adding connectors from its Muse personal AI agent to 15 outside tools and to Facebook Pages, Instagram analytics and Meta ad accounts, with Meta saying nothing is published, sent or paid for without the owner's approval. This is older news that our 10 Oct 2026 edition carried when Amazon asked to be removed from Muse; PPC Land's new analysis stresses what Meta has left unsaid.
notes: Read in full from the main session's fulltext copy. Event is 29 Sep 2026; already in the 10 Oct 2026 edition (Retail Dive via MLive, Amazon item), so the main session's 14-day duplicate check should treat it as old news.
